summary: This note describes the geographic size of New England, the northeastern U.S. region. Its six states have a combined area of 71,991.8 square miles, slightly larger than Washington state and larger than England. Maine makes up nearly half of that area, while the remaining states are among the smallest in the country.
one_line: Overview of New England's combined land area and how its states compare in size to Washington state, England and other U.S. states.
key_facts: The states of New England have a combined area of 71,991.8 square miles (186,458 km).
The combined area of New England makes the region slightly larger than the state of Washington.
The combined area of New England makes the region larger than England.
Maine alone constitutes nearly one-half of the total area of New England.
Maine is only the 39th-largest state in the U.S.
Maine is slightly smaller than Indiana.
The remaining New England states are among the smallest in the U.S.
Rhode Island is the smallest state in the U.S.
